newsitem.title: USA: Boeing may alter sole-supplier pacts - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing may alter sole-supplier pacts - WSJ.

text.p: Boeing Co may change its sole-supplier pacts with three U.S. airlines in an attempt to pacify European leaders and to remove a major obstacle to its acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said that although U.S. officials may approve the merger as soon as Tuesday, Europe continues to offer resistance and the European Union's executive commission has threatened to block it.

European antitrust officials contend that Boeing's agreements with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Delta Air Lines Inc and Continental Airlines Inc to buy planes only from Boeing over the next two decades shows that the company is already abusing its dominant position in the market.

Unnamed sources said that Boeing is considering scrapping the exclusivity provision in its agreements with the three airlines. However, it would leave the $16.9 billion in firm orders placed under those agreements intact.
That would leave those airlines free to buy other aircraft from European rival Airbus Industrie.
